_why: A cross-implementation test vector. The tunnel has two halves — serverXR mints, di.bo verifies — and every other protocol in this estate that had two halves has drifted silently with both sides' tests green: the Armenian address token, then the channel prefix. A shared vector is the cheapest thing that cannot drift, because it fails on whichever side changed. Both suites MUST assert against this file.
algorithm: base64url( 0x01 || insc16 || exp_u32be || hmac16 ), hmac = HMAC-SHA256(secret, first 21 bytes) truncated to 16 bytes
notes: The token is DETERMINISTIC, not random. Random bytes would need a server-side store; the signature IS the binding, which is why no table exists.
exp is unix MINUTES, big-endian uint32.
insc16 is the 16 raw bytes of the inscription uuid, with the 'insc-' prefix and the dashes removed.
The output is base64url with no padding — exactly Telegram's permitted ?start= alphabet (A-Za-z0-9_-). A dotted v1.<id>.<sig> form would be rejected by Telegram.

must_reject.wrong_secret: a token minted with any other secret
must_reject.hand_built: a token whose id is correct but whose hmac is zeroed — the field is world-readable, so every insc- id is public and forging must require the secret
must_reject.wrong_length: anything that is not exactly 50 base64url chars
must_reject.wrong_version: a leading byte that is not 0x01
